Get complete structural metadata of the data product.

Returns the full metadata catalog including the product definition, all models with their
schemas and properties, all metrics with their definitions, and optionally the complete
relationship graph between entities. This is the primary discovery endpoint for understanding
what data assets exist and how they relate to each other.

Set `expand=true` to include relationships in the response. Relationships are excluded by

get.description:
Generate comprehensive markdown documentation for all data product entities and optionally
chunk them for use in RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) systems and LLM applications.

Transforms your data product (products, models, metrics, fields) into structured markdown
documentation using Jinja2 templates. The documentation captures entity definitions,
relationships, dependencies, and metadata in a format that's both human-readable and
machine-processable.

Supports three output modes:
- Documents only (default): Full markdown documents without chunks
- Documents + chunks: Full documents with nested chunk arrays for hybrid search
- Chunks only: Only chunked content (useful for pure vector search scenarios)

get.description:
List all quality checks with their latest execution status.

Returns a catalog of all unique quality checks that have been executed, including check metadata
(identity, name, type, dimension, definition) and the most recent execution result. Each check's
`runs` array contains only the latest run (runs[0] if exists), showing the current status.

Use query parameters to filter checks by model names (comma-separated), column name, or dimension.
When filtering by `column_name` alone, returns checks for that column across all models. Combine
with `model_name` to scope the column filter to specific models. This provides a check-first view
of quality data, useful for discovering all checks across models and understanding their current
execution status.

To see execution history for a specific check, use the `/quality/checks/{check_identity}` endpoint.

schema.description: Comma-separated list of model names to filter checks. Omit to return all checks.

get.description:
Get execution history for a specific quality check.

Returns the complete execution history of a check across multiple runs, showing how its outcome
changed over time. The `runs` array contains all executions ordered by most recent first, with
each entry including run metadata (run_id, start_ts, end_ts) and check outcome (pass/fail/warn/error).

Use query parameters to filter runs by model name, time range (start_ts, end_ts), or limit the
number of results. This is useful for tracking check reliability over time, identifying when a
check started failing or passing, and analyzing patterns in check behavior.

To list all checks with their latest status, use the `/quality/checks` endpoint.

get.description:
Get product-level quality snapshot at a specific point in time.

Returns aggregated quality metrics across all models in the product, computed using the latest
known quality for each model up to the specified run. Quality metrics are grouped by dimension
(e.g., completeness, accuracy, timeliness) and include pass/fail/warn/error counts and pass rates.

Use `latest` as run_id to get the most recent snapshot, or provide a specific run_id for historical
time-travel queries. For each model, the system uses the most recent quality data available up to
the target run (models may have quality from different runs), then aggregates across all models.

The response includes `prev_run_id` and `next_run_id` fields for navigating backward and forward
through snapshots chronologically. The `models_included` field lists all models that contributed
to this snapshot. Quality metrics represent the entire product, not filtered to specific models.

Examples: `/quality/snapshot/latest` for the most recent snapshot, `/quality/snapshot/abc123` for
a specific historical point in time.

parameters.name: run_id

schema.description: Run ID for time-travel. Use 'latest' for the most recent snapshot.
schema.title: Run Id

parameters.description: Run ID for time-travel. Use 'latest' for the most recent snapshot.

404.description: No quality data found for the specified criteria

get.description:
Get detailed information for a specific plan deployment.

Returns complete plan information including what changed (added, removed, modified models),
which models were affected directly and indirectly, backfill requirements, execution metadata,
and links to related plans. Use this to understand what a plan deployment changed and its impact.

To list all plans, use the `/activity/timeline` endpoint with `action=plan` filter.

Get complete information for a specific run execution.

Returns unified run information including execution status, performance metrics for all executed models,
quality check results (if available), and data profiling statistics (if available). Quality checks and
profiles are grouped by model name and include all models executed in the run.

Quality and profile fields are `None` if no quality checks or profiling were performed for the run.
This is not an error condition - it simply means those features weren't enabled for that execution.

To list all runs, use the `/activity/timeline` endpoint with `action=run` filter.

Get unified timeline of plan changes and run executions.

Returns a chronological list of all plan and run activities ordered by creation time (most recent first).
Each event includes basic metadata and links to its detail page. Run events also include aggregated
quality metrics by dimension (pass/fail/warn counts and pass rates) for all models executed in that run.

Use query parameters to filter by environment, event type (plan/run), time range, or specific models.
When filtering by `model_names`, only activities affecting those models are included, but quality metrics
in run events still show all models executed in each run (not filtered to the specified models).

Plan events show what changed (models added/removed/modified). Run events show execution results and
quality metrics. Use the `_links.self` field in each event to navigate to detailed information.

post.description:
Submit source SQL query for execution.

**What this is:**
Accepts raw SQL queries and submits them for asynchronous execution via the
statement flow. Returns immediately with a statement ID for polling.

**Why this helps:**
- Execute arbitrary SQL queries against data sources
- Leverage query caching and reuse
- Monitor execution status asynchronously

**How it works:**
Validates SQL, checks cache, and submits to queue. Always returns 202 Accepted
with statement ID. Use _links to poll GET /statement/{id} for status and results.

post.description:
Submit REST semantic query for execution.

**What this is:**
Accepts REST Query format (measures, dimensions, filters) and converts it to
SQL before submitting for execution via the statement flow.

**Why this helps:**
- Query data using business-friendly REST API format
- Leverage semantic layer abstractions
- Access metrics and dimensions without writing SQL

**How it works:**
Converts REST query to SQL, then executes via statement flow. Always returns 202 Accepted. 
Use _links to poll GET /statement/{id} for status and results.

post.description:
Submit semantic SQL query for execution.

**What this is:**
Accepts semantic SQL (SQL with metric/dimension references) and converts it to
executable SQL before submitting for execution via the statement flow.

**Why this helps:**
- Write SQL using semantic layer abstractions
- Reference metrics and dimensions by name
- Leverage semantic layer optimizations

**How it works:**
Converts semantic SQL to executable SQL, then executes via statement flow. Always returns 202 Accepted. 
Use _links to poll GET /statement/{id} for status and results.

**Note:**
For MySQL client dialect transpilation, use the internal endpoint /_internal/query/semantic/sql.

post.description:
Execute GraphQL queries against the data product.

**What this is:**
Accepts GraphQL queries and executes them against the semantic layer, returning
results in GraphQL format.

**Why this helps:**
- Query data using GraphQL syntax
- Access semantic layer via GraphQL schema
- Maintain GraphQL spec compliance

**How it works:**
Processes GraphQL queries and returns results in standard GraphQL response format.
Returns GraphQL-compatible error responses on connection or timeout errors.

get.description:
Get recursive directory listing of all project files.

Returns a nested directory structure of all files and directories in the project, excluding
ignored patterns (e.g., __pycache__, .git, etc.). The structure is recursive, showing all
subdirectories and their contents.

Files and directories matching ignore patterns defined in the project configuration are excluded
from the response. Use this to browse the project structure programmatically or build file
explorer interfaces.

Get a single file with its contents.

Returns file metadata and contents for a specific file in the project. The path must be
relative to the project root and must not match any ignore patterns. Binary files return
`content=None` since they cannot be read as text.

Returns 404 if the file doesn't exist, the path is outside the project directory, or the
path matches ignore patterns. Use this to read file contents programmatically or display
file content in UIs.

ModelExec.title: ModelExec
ModelExec.description:
Execution data for a single model (pure metrics, no errors).

Timing Fields Explained:
- start_ts/end_ts: Wall-clock time (includes all overhead)
- evaluation_ms: Pure SQL evaluation duration only (sum of all batch SQL durations)

Example: If a model runs 3 batches with SQL times of 2000ms, 3000ms, 1000ms, plus 5000ms overhead:
- evaluation_ms = 6000 milliseconds (SQL only)
- end_ts - start_ts = 11000 milliseconds (total wall-clock)
- Overhead = 5000 milliseconds (network, Python processing, etc.)

Relationship.description:
Relationship between nodes in the metadata graph.

Represents connections between models, fields, and metrics with
type-specific metadata.

RelationshipType.title: RelationshipType
RelationshipType.description:
Relationship type enumeration.

Relationship names are lowercase snake_case and unique per (from_type, to_type) pair.
Each (from_type, to_type) combination has its own unique relationship name.
Enum keys are uppercase, values are lowercase snake_case.
